important_instructions: AFMS has announced 120 SSC Medical Officer vacancies. 90 vacancies are for male candidates and 30 for female candidates. Applications are open from 9 November to 18 November 2026. Final MBBS Part-I and II must have been passed in not more than two attempts. Internship must be completed by 30 September 2026. Permanent medical registration is required. NEET PG eligibility and shortlisting conditions must be satisfied. MBBS applicants must meet the notified under-30 age condition. Eligible PG doctors must meet the notified under-35 age condition. The application processing fee is Rs. 200 and is non-refundable. NEET PG percentile is converted into calculated marks out of 200. The interview carries 50 marks, including applicable NCC weightage. The minimum qualifying interview score is 50%. Separate male and female final merit lists are prepared. Interview-eligible candidates must undergo medical examination. The interview is tentatively scheduled from 2 December 2026. Initial Short Service Commission tenure is five years. Selected officers may be posted anywhere in India or abroad. Original certificates and five attestation forms must be available for interview verification. Applicants should monitor the official website and registered email for updates.

content_sections.heading: AFMS Medical Officer Vacancy 2026 - 120 Posts
content_sections.text: AFMS has announced 120 Medical Officer vacancies under the Short Service Commission, divided between male and female candidates. The notification provides separate male and female vacancy allocations and separate merit lists for selection. It does not provide a further specialty-wise or social-category-wise vacancy breakup.

content_sections.heading: AFMS SSC Medical Officer Recruitment 2026 Notification PDF
content_sections.text: The Armed Forces Medical Services has issued the detailed 2026 recruitment notification for 120 Medical Officer (Short Service Commission) vacancies . The six-page notification contains the complete eligibility requirements, NEET PG shortlisting formula, interview process, age conditions, application fee, salary, service tenure, promotion provisions and document requirements. Official Recruitment Website: AFMS Medical Officer Recruitment 2026 The detailed notification should be accessed through the official recruitment portal. A separately verified public direct URL for the six-page PDF has not been established.

content_sections.heading: AFMS Medical Officer Recruitment 2026 Eligibility Criteria
content_sections.text: Candidates must possess a medical qualification recognized under the National Medical Commission Act, 2019, and permanent medical registration with the competent medical council. The notification requires applicants to have appeared in NEET PG during 2025 or 2026, subject to its separate provision for civilian doctors holding postgraduate medical qualifications. Existing civilian PG doctors are not required to appear in NEET PG again. Their previously obtained NEET PG marks will be considered for shortlisting. Important: The notice does not impose a separate minimum NEET PG percentile for application eligibility. However, NEET PG performance is used to rank candidates for interview shortlisting. Yes. Candidates with a recognized MBBS degree can apply without MD, MS or another PG degree, provided they satisfy the MBBS attempt limit, internship completion, permanent registration, NEET PG and age conditions. Yes. Candidates holding recognized postgraduate medical qualifications can apply. Civilian PG doctors are covered by the notification's provision allowing previously obtained NEET PG marks to be used without appearing in NEET PG again. Candidates still pursuing a PG degree must have their final result declared by 18 November 2026 and possess the required qualification documents for verification. Yes. Applicants must have completed their compulsory medical internship on or before 30 September 2026 . Candidates whose internships were completed after this deadline are not eligible under the notified conditions. No. The notification requires candidates to have passed their final MBBS Part-I and Part-II examinations in not more than two attempts. Applicants must submit the relevant final MBBS attempt certificate or transcript supporting this eligibility condition.

content_sections.text: Selected candidates will be commissioned in the rank of Captain or equivalent rank in the Navy or Air Force , under Level 10B of the Defence Pay Matrix. Salary Clarification: Rs. 76,800 represents the combined basic pay and Military Service Pay, not the final take-home salary. Applicable allowances, benefits, taxes and deductions depend on service rules and posting location. 60 days of annual leave. 20 days of casual leave annually. Leave Travel Concession (LTC). Medical services for the officer and eligible family members, including dependent parents. Group insurance. Canteen Stores Department (CSD) facilities. Subsidized accommodation and associated facilities, as applicable. Ration or ration allowance under the applicable service conditions. PG allowance or specialist pay for eligible officers.

content_sections.heading: AFMS SSC Medical Officer Selection Process 2026
content_sections.text: Selection involves NEET PG-based shortlisting, interview, medical examination and preparation of separate male and female final merit lists . Online application and eligibility scrutiny. Shortlisting using calculated NEET PG marks. Viva-voce / Personal Interview. Special Medical Examination Board. Final merit list preparation. Joining instructions for medically fit candidates selected against available vacancies. AFMS converts the candidate's NEET PG percentile into a score out of 200 for interview shortlisting. Calculated NEET PG Marks = NEET PG Percentile × 2 The above values are illustrative applications of the official calculation formula, not actual selection cut-offs. If the original NEET PG result was declared using an absolute score, AFMS will first determine the percentile based on the candidate's merit position and then calculate the equivalent marks out of 200. Separate shortlisting lists are prepared for male and female candidates. The interview carries a maximum of 50 marks , including weightage for the highest applicable NCC certificate. Only the highest eligible NCC certificate is considered. Candidates cannot add the marks for A, B and C certificates together. Candidates must obtain at least 50% of the interview marks , equivalent to 25 out of 50, to qualify for further consideration. Qualifying in the interview does not automatically guarantee selection or commissioning. The final merit list combines the calculated NEET PG marks out of 200 and interview marks out of 50, giving a maximum combined score of 250. Separate male and female merit lists are prepared. Joining instructions are issued to selected candidates who are declared medically fit, according to the available vacancies.

content_sections.heading: AFMS Medical Officer Interview Date and Venue 2026
content_sections.text: Interviews are tentatively scheduled from 2 December 2026 onwards at Army Hospital (Research & Referral), Delhi Cantonment. Candidates attending an AFMS interview for the first time are eligible for the prescribed to-and-fro AC III / AC Chair Car railway fare or Government non-AC bus fare from their normal place of residence. No travelling allowance is payable to candidates residing within the municipal limits of the interview location.

rows.details: Available at Least One Week Before Interview Commencement

content_sections.heading: AFMS Medical Officer Medical Examination 2026
content_sections.text: Interview-qualified candidates must undergo a medical examination by the Special Medical Examination Board (SMB) constituted by the Directorate General Armed Forces Medical Services. Candidates declared medically unfit may seek an Appeal Medical Board according to the prescribed procedure. A Review Medical Board may be permitted at the discretion of DGAFMS. Final medical fitness is established only after approval of the medical examination documents.

content_sections.heading: AFMS SSC Medical Officer Tenure 2026
content_sections.text: The initial Short Service Commission tenure for fresh civilian entrants is five years . Extensions depend on willingness to continue, availability of vacancies, eligibility and applicable service policies. Extension is not automatic. Eligible SSC officers may receive opportunities to appear for the Departmental Permanent Commission examination under the applicable rules. The notification provides up to three chances after completing two years of service and before completing nine and a half years, subject to the prescribed eligibility conditions and attempt restrictions. Important: Permanent Commission is not guaranteed by selection into the SSC Medical Officer recruitment.

content_sections.text: Promotions are subject to the applicable service and eligibility conditions. The notification also describes further career progression under Permanent Commission and opportunities for postgraduate and super-specialty training according to service rules.

content_sections.text: Eligible candidates can apply online for 120 AFMS Medical Officer vacancies between 9 November and 18 November 2026 . content_sections.heading: How to Apply Online for AFMS SSC Medical Officer Recruitment 2026?
content_sections.text: Visit the official recruitment portal at join.afms.gov.in . Read the Medical Officer (Short Service Commission) Recruitment 2026 notification. Click NEW REGISTRATION . Follow the registration instructions displayed on the website. Enter the required personal and contact details. Provide the prescribed MBBS and postgraduate qualification information, where applicable. Enter medical registration and internship completion information as requested. Provide NEET PG examination information according to the notified eligibility provisions. Upload the required photograph and documents. Review the entered details and supporting certificates carefully. Pay the non-refundable Rs. 200 application processing fee through the available online payment method. Complete the online application submission by 18 November 2026 . Save the payment transaction number. Download and retain the completed application form and available acknowledgement. Monitor the official website and registered email for shortlisting and interview instructions. Important: Applicants must ensure that their online information agrees with the original documents. Incorrect, incomplete or unsupported information can result in rejection.

content_sections.heading: Documents Required for AFMS Medical Officer Recruitment 2026
content_sections.text: Candidates must upload the prescribed documents while applying and produce original records with two photocopies during the interview verification process. The notification specifies exact file-size limits for the photograph and date-of-birth document. Candidates must follow the current application portal instructions for the remaining upload fields. Downloaded interview admit card and application form. Original Class 10 certificate or accepted municipal birth certificate. Aadhaar card. Permanent medical registration certificate. Internship completion certificate. MBBS degree certificate and PG degree certificate, if applicable. Final MBBS Part-I and II attempt certificate or transcript. NEET PG scorecard. No Objection Certificate from the present employer, if applicable. NCC certificate, if claiming the applicable weightage. National Board of Examinations certificate for Foreign Medical Graduates, where applicable. Passport for Foreign Medical Graduates, where applicable. Gazette notification or supporting document for a name change after Class 10, where applicable. Ten recent passport-size photographs. Photo identification and address proof. Five completed and duly attested copies of the prescribed attestation form. Candidates must bring the original documents and two photocopies of each applicable certificate. Where an original document is deposited with another institution, the specific deposit-certificate and attested-copy procedure in the notification applies. Candidates must bring five copies of the prescribed attestation form , completed and attested by the competent authority, as specified in the official instructions. Failure to provide the prescribed attestation forms may result in rejection at the interview stage.
